mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a given month leads to a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as investors anticipate higher borrowing costs eroding equity valuation multiples.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the same month after the rate hike (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not revert below 5.25% within 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 6.5% for two consecutive months is associated with a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return due to expectations of slower wage growth and reduced corporate hiring.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in at least 70% of similar UNRATE-up periods (binomial test), or UNRATE reverts to ≤ 6.5% within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly composite of HOUST and INDPRO both exceed their 12-month moving averages by at least 10%, it signals robust consumer and production momentum that drives a positive S&P 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > HOUST_12MA and INDPRO > INDPRO_12MA, both by ≥ 10%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically significant (p > 0.10) in 80% of such dual-momentum events (bootstrap), or either HOUST or INDPRO falls below its 12-month MA within 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in PAYEMS of at least 5% while RSAFS rises by more than 15% indicates easing supply constraints in the services sector, which is associated with a positive S&P 60-day forward return as demand recovers.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases ≥ 5% for two consecutive months AND RSAFS increases ≥ 15% in the same months
regime_hint: Transition from supply bottleneck to supply flexibility
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of such events (binomial test), or the PAYEMS decline reverses before the RSAFS increase stabilizes.

mechanism_narrative: During a 3-month period of consecutive FEDFUNDS declines below the prior month's value, the S&P 20-day forward return is positive as investors anticipate future rate cuts and liquidity injections.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive in 60% of such 3-month decline windows (bootstrap), or FEDFUNDS does not sustain a downward trend beyond 4 months.

mechanism_narrative: A one-time monthly spike in PAYEMS above 140,000 while UNRATE remains below 5%, occurring during a low-inflation regime, predicts a positive S&P 5-day forward return as hiring accelerates without wage pressure.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 140,000 AND UNRATE < 5% AND PAYEMS > PAYEMS_prev_month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive in 70% of such events (bootstrapped confidence interval excludes zero), or UNRATE rises above 5% within 10 days.

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO falls below its 6-month moving average for three consecutive months without a compensating rise in HOUST, it indicates softening manufacturing momentum and is associated with a negative S&P 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < INDPRO_6MA for three consecutive months AND HOUST does not exceed HOUST_6MA in those months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in 80% of such events (bootstrap), or INDPRO recovers above its 6-month MA within 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in CPIAUCSL by at least 0.3% while FEDFUNDS remains below 1% signals disinflation that is supportive of equity valuations, predicting a positive S&P 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases ≥ 0.3% for three consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS < 1%
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not positive in 75% of such disinflation episodes (binomial test), or CPIAUCSL rises above the prior 3-month trend before the 60-day window closes.
